newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-FACTS AND FIGURES OF EUROPEAN CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FACTS AND FIGURES OF EUROPEAN CUP FINAL.

text.p: Facts and Figures of Wednesday's European Cup Final between holders Juventus of Italy and Borussia Dortmund of Germany:

Wednesday's final is the 42nd since the competition began in the 1955-56 season. Real Madrid, who last won the trophy 31 years ago are still the most successful club winning the competition six times. Italy have been the most successful nation with nine wins, followed by England with eight.

This is the second time Juventus and Borussia Dortmund have met in a European final in the Nineties. In 1992-93 Juventus beat Borussia 3-1 away and 3-0 at home to win the UEFA Cup by a record aggregate score of 6-1. Five former players are now at Dortmund and four of them -- Julio Cesar, Juergen Kohler, Andreas Moeller and Stefan Reuter, played for Juve against Dortmund during that final. The fifth player is Paulo Sousa.

This is the fourth meeting between the two clubs in Europe -- and Juventus have won every time. As well as the 1993 UEFA Cup Final, Juventus beat Borussia Dortmund 4-3 on aggregate (2-2, 2-1) in the 1995 UEFA Cup semifinals and 3-1 and 2-1 in last season's Champions' League.

Juventus's appearance means Italian clubs have competed in eight European Cup finals in the last nine years and for the last six years in sucession. AC Milan reached the final in 1989 and 1990, Sampdoria in 1992, AC Milan in 1993, 1994, 1995 followed by Juventus in 1996 and now 1997.

Juventus are competing in their fifth final and have not scored more than one goal in any of their previous four. In 1973 Ajax beat them 1-0; in 1985 Hamburg beat them 1-0; in 1985 Juventus beat Liverpool 1-0, and in 1996 Juventus drew 1-1 with Ajax then won the cup 4-2 on penalties.

Borussia Dortmund are competing in their first European Cup Final and are the first German team to reach the final since Bayern Munich lost to Porto in 1987. They are attempting to become the first German team to win the Cup since Hamburg beat Juventus in 1983.
Borussia were the first German team to win a European trophy in 1966 when they defeated Liverpool 2-1 after extra time in the European Cup Winners' Cup Final in Glasgow.

Munich is hosting the European Cup Final for the third time and on both previous occasions the final produced only one goal. In 1979 Nottingham Forest defeated Malmo 1-0 and in 1993 Marseille beat AC Milan 1-0 with current Juventus player Didier Deschamps captaining the French side. The stadium has also hosted the 1974 World Cup Final, the 1988 European Championship final and the 1972 Olympic Games.

Juventus are bidding to become the ninth club to retain the trophy and to emulate the feats of Italian rivals Inter Milan (champions in 1964 and 1965) and AC Milan (1989 and 1990). The six other clubs who have won the trophy at least twice in succession are Real Madrid (1956-60), Benfica (1961, 1962), Ajax (1971-73), Bayern Munich (1974-76), Liverpool (1977, 1978) and Nottingham Forest (1979, 1980).

Juventus, who clinched the Italian title on Friday, are also bidding to become the 19th club to win the European Cup and their own domestic championship in the same season. Surprisingly the great Real Madrid team of the 1950s only managed that feat twice, in 1957 and 1958. The last team to do it were Ajax in 1995.

With Borussia playing in Munich, Wednesday's final will be the 10th time that the match has been staged in the home country of one of the finalists. On six of the previous nine occasions the team from the home country won -- 1957: Real Madrid (Madrid); 1965 Inter Milan (Milan); 1968: Manchester United (London); 1972 Ajax (Rotterdam); 1978: Liverpool (London); 1996: Juventus (Rome). The three occasions the "home" team lost were: 1956 Reims (Paris); 1984: AS Roma (Rome); 1986 Barcelona (Seville).

The first eight finals from 1956 to 1963 produced 42 goals -- including 10 in the 1960 final when Real Madrid beat Germans Eintracht Frankfurt 7-3. In comparison only 14 goals have been scored in the last nine finals.
